conventions.convention: The CMDP has nonempty finite states, finite nonempty state-dependent action sets, a finite reward alphabet, a normalized joint reward/next-state law, bounded transition costs, a common initial distribution, and discount 0 ≤ γ < 1.
State distributions are column vectors; Kπ(s′,s) gives the transition probability from s to s′. The occupancy is dπ = (1−γ) Σ(t≥0) γ^t μπ_t.
Jg is the unnormalized expected discounted transition-signal sum, starting at time zero. Feasibility means Jci ≤ bi for every cost and asserts no per-trajectory bound.

Finite-action TV is half the ℓ1 difference. KL uses natural logarithms and direction new policy relative to old policy. Average KL omits zero-weight states and is infinite for a support violation at a positive-weight state.
For arbitrary bounded baseline f, L averages the new-policy residual minus the old-policy residual under dπ; the error coefficient uses the maximum absolute new-policy statewise residual.
The TV performance bounds are choice-free. The KL branch assumes AC and explicitly interprets infinite average KL as trivial extended bounds, including when the formal error coefficient vanishes.

The update uses fixed common policy support on an open positive-dimensional parameter domain, local C2 regularity, positive sampled denominators, normalized nonnegative weights, fixed real estimates, an exact quadratic subproblem with lexicographic tie-breaking, and a finite ordered backtracking budget.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite discounted CMDP and stationary policy, every finite-time state-mass vector and the normalized discounted occupancy are probability distributions. For every B ≥ 0 and transition signal bounded in absolute value by B, Jg converges absolutely and |Jg| ≤ B/(1−γ).

For a finite discounted CMDP, bounded transition signal g, bounded baseline f and stationary policies π,π′, Jgπ′−Jgπ = Lπ,f^g(π′)/(1−γ) + Σs(dπ′(s)−dπ(s)) δbar_f^{g,π′}(s)/(1−γ), where L averages δbar_f^{g,π′}−δbar_f^{g,π} under dπ.
For a finite discounted CMDP and stationary policies π,π′, ‖dπ′−dπ‖1 ≤ 2γ/(1−γ) Σs dπ(s) TVs(π′,π).

Assume AC. For a probability distribution d on a finite nonempty state set and probability distributions qs,ps on finite nonempty action sets, Σs d(s) TV(qs,ps) ≤ √(K/2), where K = Σ{s:d(s)>0} d(s) DKL(qs‖ps), with infinite K allowed.

For a finite discounted CMDP, bounded g,f and stationary π,π′, the return difference lies between Lπ,f^g(π′)/(1−γ) ± 2γε_f^g(π′)/(1−γ)^2 Σs dπ(s) TVs(π′,π). Under AC, replacing the average TV by the square root of half the average directional KL preserves both inequalities; infinite average KL gives trivial extended bounds.

Under the sample update's inputs and assumptions and nonnegative integer budget L, the update has a unique mathematical output. A feasible positive-definite quadratic program has a unique lexicographically least maximizer; the nonzero single-cost recovery proposal uniquely minimizes the linearized cost on the trust ellipsoid. Once exact subproblem operations have been performed, backtracking uses at most L+1 candidate tests. These properties do not certify population costs, population KL, improvement or convergence.

concerns.concern: The Remarks references label for alg-constrained-policy-optimization says “The sample-based update, quadratic approximation, CG solves, line search, and optional cost shaping.” The cited algorithm specifies an exact finite-data subproblem and contains no conjugate-gradient procedure. CG belongs to the practical implementation discussed in the cited paper, whose §6.1 explicitly describes approximate conjugate-gradient computations. The reference label conflates those two procedures; the remark's mathematical caveat remains sound.
